summary: SDK auto-refresh + retry interleaving causes duplicate tool/function invocations for long-running chat sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external tool (webhook/job) invocations during long-running chat sessions when the SDK's automatic credential refresh runs concurrently with client-side retry/backoff. This appears most frequently on Python services that use pre-fork multiprocessing (gunicorn/uvicorn with workers) or multiprocess workers that do not serialize refreshes across processes.

Impact:
- Customer sees duplicate side-effects (two webhook POSTs, duplicate downstream DB writes) for ~1% of long-running sessions.
- Duplication causes customer upstream dedupe logic to trigger alerts and in rare cases billing mismatches.

Environment:
- Customer: NovaDocs (dedicated)
- SDKs: python-sdk v1.4.2 in web service (gunicorn with 4 workers, pre-fork), also reproduced locally with multiprocess test harness.
- Backend: Redwood hosted inference, redwood-alpha-1 model pinned.
- Region: us-east-1

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Start a long-running streaming chat with function/tool calling enabled.
2) Simulate a transient 5xx from the router so the client retry/backoff activates.
3) Force token refresh to occur during the retry window by shortening token TTL / provoking background refresh. Customer shortened SDK token TTL to 30s to force frequent refresh.
4) Observe duplicate external tool invocations (two distinct requests received by downstream webhook) correlated to the same logical response generation.

Example minimal repro (pseudo):
- app starts under gunicorn pre-fork mode (4 workers)
- each request uses a shared SDK client created at import-time
- background refresh runs on a timer in each worker process
- client retry middleware replays an in-flight funcall when a transient network error happens

Expected behavior:
- Retries should not result in duplicate external side-effects when idempotency tokens or confirmation semantics are present. Background refresh should not cause token/idempotency salt rotation that invalidates earlier confirmations in the retry window.

Actual behavior:
- Two calls arrive at downstream webhook ~100-400ms apart with different api-correlation ids but the same logical model output. The SDK appears to re-send the same funcall after a refresh boundary while the original attempt is still being retried by the runtime.

Logs / artifacts provided by customer (sanitized):
- webhook received: X-Redwood-Correlation: rwd-abc-001, rwd-abc-002
- client logs: "refresh_detected: acquiring new token; idempotency_salt rotated"
- server trace: "retry_middleware: requeue funcall (attempt=2)"

Temporary workaround suggested to customer (applied locally):
- Disable SDK auto-refresh in multi-process workers and inject a single process to manage token refresh and share token via a small in-memory endpoint or use an external refresh process.
- Alternatively increase token TTL so refresh windows do not align with retry windows.
investigation:
Initial triage by Support: reproduced with a small multiprocess harness using python-sdk v1.4.2. Repro steps reliability ~10/100 runs when token TTL is 30s and transient error introduced during streaming.

SRE/serving-runtime notes: observed that when a token refresh completes in-process the SDK rotates an internal 'idempotency_salt' used to derive per-action dedupe keys. If a retry is in-flight while the salt flips, the SDK may construct a new request that the router considers distinct; because confirmation tokens for earlier attempts were tied to the old salt, the downstream acknowledgement flow does not dedupe.

Repro harness summary:
- Spawn 4 worker processes (multiprocessing.Process) each with a local SDK client instance created post-fork.
- Create a stream, trigger a synthetic router 502 on the first chunk to force client-side retry, then trigger local refresh.
- Downstream test server receives duplicate POSTs with different X-Idempotency-Hash headers.

Hypothesis: race between per-process background refresh (no cross-process coordination) and retry/backoff window causes idempotency key inconsistency leading to duplicate side-effects.

Related investigation threads: Slack #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0123456), internal runbook link (above).
comments: 2026-03-11 - Aisha Rao (Support): Ticket created after customer filed through console support form. Captured repro artifacts and initial logs. Marked P1 due to duplicate side-effects causing customer alerts.

2026-03-11 - NovaDocs (Customer, Jenna Park): We see duplicates mostly during high-latency windows. Disabling auto-refresh in workers eliminated duplicates in our staging tests. Happy to provide access to test cluster logs if needed.

2026-03-12 - Diego Martinez (Eng): Reproduced locally with provided harness. Confirmed idempotency_salt rotation correlates with duplicates. Created a unit test that fails consistently when salt is rotated mid-retry. Adding tracing for idempotency key generation to PR notes.

2026-03-12 - SRE (Marta Alvarez): Observed related spikes in retry counts on the customer's dedicated pool around TTL boundaries. No evidence of server-side duplicate delivery; duplicates originate client-side due to mismatched dedupe keys.

2026-03-13 - Diego Martinez (Eng): Proposed short-term SDK patch: protect refresh with a process-global lock and avoid rotating idempotency_salt until inflight confirmations have settled (configurable grace window). Will open PR for python-sdk with tests and add a config flag 'refresh_lock_mode' defaulting to 'auto' that supports 'process-lock' for pre-fork deployments.

2026-03-13 - Aisha Rao (Support): Notified customer of proposed fix and requested permission to deploy a canary to their dedicated pool once PR passes CI. Customer approved canary testing after hours.
2026-03-13 - NovaDocs (Customer, Jenna Park): Approved canary. Also asked for guidance to make their setup safe until the SDK patch is live.
next_steps:
1) Eng: land python-sdk PR that serializes refresh in pre-fork/multiprocess modes and adds a configurable grace window for idempotency_salt rotation (tracking PR #812). Target branch: release/1.4.x.
2) QE: add the multiprocess repro harness to CI as a flaky test guard.
3) SRE: schedule canary in NovaDocs' dedicated pool outside peak hours and monitor duplicates metric.
4) Docs/Support: publish short guidance for customers running pre-fork servers: create client post-fork, use external refresh, or enable 'process-lock' refresh mode until patch released.
5) Follow-up: consider sharing a cross-language design for idempotency salt lifecycle across SDKs (python/ts/go).
resolution: In Progress - patch PR opened (see related_github_prs). Customer-approved canary pending. Final resolution will be closing when canary shows no duplicates for 48h and PR released to customers.
